draft.title: The respiratory system
card: Air enters through the nose or mouth and moves down the trachea (windpipe). The trachea splits into two bronchi, one to each lung.
Inside each lung, the bronchi branch into smaller tubes that end in tiny air sacs called alveoli. There are millions of alveoli in the lungs.
Each alveolus is wrapped in tiny blood vessels called capillaries. Oxygen passes from the air in the alveolus into the blood. Carbon dioxide passes from the blood into the air.
The blood carries the oxygen to cells, which use it to release energy from food. Carbon dioxide is a waste, and it leaves the body when we breathe out.
draft.remember: Oxygen goes into the blood at the alveoli, and carbon dioxide comes out.

a.q: Where in the lungs does oxygen pass from the air into the blood?
a.why: Oxygen passes into the blood in the alveoli, which are wrapped in capillaries. The bronchi are tubes that carry air to the alveoli, so gas does not pass into the blood there.
a.clue: Look for the tiny air sacs wrapped in capillaries.

b.q: Leila breathes in. Which list shows the order the air passes through these parts on its way to the blood?
b.why: Air moves down the trachea, which splits into the bronchi, and the bronchi lead to the alveoli where gases pass into the blood. The order bronchi then trachea is tempting, but the trachea is the single tube that splits into the two bronchi.
b.clue: The windpipe splits into two tubes, and those tubes end in air sacs.
